title: S719 Outcome Reconciliation
methodology: Direct grep (Select-String) on all 5 pack files for CognitiveLevel, Difficulty, DifficultyScore, question_state, and QuestionID. Cross-checked against S719 analytics package, session summary, misalignment census, distribution analytics, reliability retest results, final verification, and governance audit. B/C/D unchanged status verified via Agent M hash comparison and file modification timestamps.

claim_244_misalignments.evidence: Pack A: 156 Evaluate→Understand CL changes + concurrent Easy→Moderate-Easy difficulty changes = all S718-flagged Pack A items resolved. Pack E: 76 Difficult@Remember→Moderate-Easy@Understand (Agent C Block-C) + all 386 Remember→Understand = all S718-flagged Pack E items resolved. However, S719 Distribution Analytics (Agent I) and Analytics Package (Agent K) both projected 12 additional changes in Packs B/C/D (B:3, C:6, D:3 Evaluate→Understand) that were NEVER EXECUTED. SESSION_SUMMARY §'Files NOT Modified' line confirms B/C/D untouched. Agent M hash verification confirms B/C/D hashes unchanged from T0. Additionally, Agent A's misalignment census identified 1,604 total DCS §3 misalignments; S719 addressed only the 244 severe S718-blocklist subset. The remaining ~1,360 moderate misalignments in B/C/D remain. Verdict: 232 of 244 severe items actually fixed (Packs A+E); 12 B/C/D items counted in reports but not executed on disk.

claim_72_pct_agreement.evidence: Agent H's reliability retest reports: recalibrated items = 72.0% CL agreement vs 46.0% for controls (+26pp improvement). However, this was measured by a mechanical DCS §3 classifier (stem-only, no distractor visibility), NOT by blinded human reviewers. The SESSION_SUMMARY misleadingly states '72% CL agreement' without noting this is a computational classifier, not human judgment. Manual review of 39 items with full choices visible achieved 84.6% CL agreement with the file. The 72% figure is conservative (underestimates actual human agreement due to distractor-blind methodology). The +26pp gap between recalibrated and control items supports that S719 improved calibration consistency.

verdict_detail: 9 of 10 claims are VERIFIED or PARTIALLY VERIFIED. The 10th claim (B/C/D unchanged) is VERIFIED. The core S719 execution was sound: 542 items correctly modified across Packs A and E. CognitiveLevel coverage confirmed at 2,500/2,500. Governance guard confirmed 20/20 PASS. Certification states preserved (2,181 total). However, S719's internal reporting contains systematic errors: the Analytics Package and Distribution Analytics both project B/C/D changes that were never executed, inflating pool-wide totals by 12 items (0.5%). The '72% reviewer agreement' claim is algorithmically derived (stem-only classifier), not human reviewer agreement (which was actually 84.6%). The '244→0 severe misalignments' claim is accurate for modified files (Packs A+E) but not pool-wide (12 B/C/D items still carry their pre-S719 misalignments). Additionally, the pool now has ~93% Understand+Apply cognitive spread — a 31.2pp Understand overcorrection above the 15% CAQS target flagged by S719's own analytics.
